nodes.title: Commuting coordinate directions with constant parameter
nodes.statement: Frame consists of d k-linear derivations δ_i:R→R, pairwise commuting on every a∈R, with δ_i(λ)=0. This is a specified affine frame, not a definition of a general differential site.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
proofSteps: Use the pinned Derivation carrier and record its pairwise commutation and constant-parameter equations.
Zero derivations give Frame.zero. On k[X_0,…,X_(d−1)], partial derivatives give Frame.polynomial with constant parameter C(c).
Prove polynomial commutation on monomials: successive removal of i,j has the same coefficient in both orders, including i=j; extend by k-linearity. Constants differentiate to zero.
Frame.one keeps the directions and uses δ_i(1)=0. No invertibility of λ is assumed.
acceptance: λ=X_0 with δ_0=∂_0 is excluded over Q since δ_0λ=1.
Zero directions are allowed, but are not universal differential forms.

nodes.title: Affine coordinate parameter connection
nodes.statement: For a fixed Frame F, Connection is a family A_i∈Mat_V(R). It encodes D_i(s)=λδ_i(s)+A_i s before imposing flatness. F is an explicit type parameter: changing the directions or parameter is not a silent type identification.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Use the matrix family as the sole data field.
Keep F explicitly in the structure declaration even though the matrix field alone does not mention F.
Construct zero matrices. Extensionality and constructor projection follow from the product representation.
acceptance: No flatness or nilpotence is imposed on an arbitrary Connection.
Any one-direction rank-one matrix family is accepted, including a nonzero scalar.

nodes.title: Coordinate parameter differential operator
nodes.statement: Define the k-linear operator (D_i s)_v=λδ_i(s_v)+(A_i s)_v. It satisfies D_i(a s)=aD_i(s)+λδ_i(a)s and is generally not R-linear.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Apply the derivation in each coordinate, multiply by λ and add the matrix-vector action.
k-linearity follows from derivation k-linearity and R-linear matrix multiplication.
Expand δ_i(a s_v) using Leibniz and scalar commutation to get precisely one λ in the scalar derivative term.
acceptance: Zero matrices give λδ, not the zero operator in general.
At λ=1 the scalar derivative is the ordinary connection term.

nodes.title: Coordinate curvature matrix
nodes.statement: Define κ_ij=λδ_i(A_j)−λδ_j(A_i)+A_i A_j−A_j A_i with entrywise derivatives. In a genuine polynomial coordinate chart the two-form is Σ_(i<j)κ_ij dx_i∧dx_j.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Construct the displayed matrix expression using entrywise derivations.
Unfold to show κ_ii=0, κ_ji=−κ_ij and vanishing curvature for zero matrices.
For E12,E21 multiply E12 E21=E11 and E21 E12=E22; constant matrices have zero derivatives.
acceptance: On Q[x,y], E12 dx+E21 dy has curvature diag(1,−1)dx∧dy.
The zero-direction Q test reproduces the same matrix coefficient without claiming universal forms.

nodes.title: Commutator is curvature action
nodes.statement: For every c,i,j and s∈R^V, D_i(D_j(s))−D_j(D_i(s))=κ_ij s.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Expand both compositions, including derivatives of λ and all matrix entries.
The second derivatives cancel by Frame.commute. Terms λδ_i(λ)δ_j(s) vanish by Frame.constant.
Use Leibniz inside finite sums; mixed A_iδ_j(s) terms cancel and remaining entries equal κ_ij s.
acceptance: Without δλ=0 an extra term is λ(δ_iλ·δ_j(s)−δ_jλ·δ_i(s)).
The E12/E21 commutator acts by diag(1,−1).

nodes.title: Flatness of the coordinate model
nodes.statement: Connection.IsFlat means κ_ij=0 for every i,j. It is equivalent to pairwise commuting D_i on every section, and does not assert nilpotence.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Define the predicate by the explicit curvature equalities.
The commutator theorem proves one direction.
For the converse evaluate the zero operator on each coordinate basis vector; every column of κ_ij vanishes.
For d=1 the only curvature is diagonal and hence zero.
acceptance: A scalar Higgs coefficient 1 on A¹_Q is flat but not nilpotent.
Two directions with E12,E21 fail flatness.

nodes.title: Coordinate change by an invertible matrix
nodes.statement: For a matrix unit G and the convention s′=Gs, define A′_i=G A_i G^−1−λδ_i(G)G^−1. The associated operator is G D_i G^−1 on the new component column.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Differentiate G G^−1=I to get δ_i(G^−1)=−G^−1δ_i(G)G^−1.
Expand G D_i(G^−1s′): its derivative coefficient is λ and its matrix coefficient has the displayed minus sign.
Its operator commutator is G[D_i,D_j]G^−1. Use the commutator node and coordinate basis evaluation to identify κ′_ij=Gκ_ijG^−1.
Invertibility of G proves preservation and reflection of curvature vanishing.
acceptance: The fixed convention is s′=Gs; the opposite convention changes the formula.
Gauge of zero matrices need not have zero matrices when λδG≠0.

nodes.title: Tensor with the same parameter
nodes.statement: For models c on R^V and b on R^W with the same F and λ, construct the free model on R^(V×W) with matrices A_i⊗I_W+I_V⊗B_i, using the Kronecker product. Its parameter is λ, not 2λ.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Use the standard free-coordinate tensor identification and define the Kronecker sum.
Entrywise differentiate; the cross commutators cancel since A⊗I commutes with I⊗B. The remaining curvature is κ_c⊗I+I⊗κ_b.
On elementary tensors, λδ(s⊗t)=λδ(s)⊗t+s⊗λδ(t). Scalar balancing identifies the derivative term represented in either factor, so one λ occurs.
Vanishing of both input curvatures implies vanishing of the tensor curvature; no converse is claimed.
acceptance: Input parameters must agree.
The balanced tensor scalar Leibniz rule has one λ derivative term.

nodes.title: Coordinate dual parameter connection
nodes.statement: Identify the dual of R^V with row coefficients transposed to a column, and define the dual matrix as −A_iᵀ. Keep the same F and λ.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Expand the evaluation-pairing equation λδ_i(φ(s))=D_dual,i(φ)(s)+φ(D_i(s)); its coefficient terms force −A_iᵀ.
Entrywise differentiation and reversal of products under transpose give κ_dual,ij=−κ_ijᵀ.
Double transposition recovers A, and curvature vanishing is preserved.
acceptance: Omitting the minus sign breaks compatibility with evaluation.
This coordinate identification is only for finite free modules, not a claimed sheaf-duality construction.

nodes.title: Rescaling an invertible parameter
nodes.statement: For u∈R× and F with λ=u, define rescale(c) on F.one by matrices u^−1A_i. Its operator is u^−1D_i and curvature u^−2κ_ij; its scalar Leibniz coefficient is 1.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Differentiate u u^−1=1 and use δ_i(u)=0 to obtain δ_i(u^−1)=0.
Retain the same directions with parameter 1 and multiply every coefficient matrix by u^−1.
The new operator is δ_i(s)+u^−1A_i s=u^−1D_i(s). Expanding curvature scales derivative and commutator terms by u^−2.
Invertibility makes flatness equivalent. Merely changing λ's type while leaving A unscaled is incorrect.
acceptance: Over Q[X], the zero-matrix λ=2 model maps X to 2; rescaling maps X to 1.
λ=0 and nonunit parameters do not admit this operation.

nodes.title: Joint word nilpotence of Higgs coefficients
nodes.statement: At λ=0, JointNilpotent(c,N) means N>0 and A_(i1)…A_(iN)=0 for every direction word of length N. This is a separate finite bound; no rank-one-zero assertion over nonreduced R is made.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Use all words of length N, not exterior products, and require N>0.
Zero matrices satisfy bound 1; one-letter words show that bound 1 iff every A_i=0.
For the dual a product equals (−1)^N times the transpose of the reversed original word, hence the same bound holds.
Compute E12²=0≠E12 and scalar ε²=0≠ε examples. The scalar 1 has nonzero word product at every positive length.
acceptance: Scalar 1 in one direction over Q is flat but has no finite bound.
For ε²=0≠ε in nonreduced R, a rank-one coefficient ε is nonzero with bound 2.
Intrinsic finite-filtration comparison and tensor nilpotence bounds remain gaps.
